name: Speech Clarity
definition: The ability to speak clearly so others can understand you.

benchmark.name: Blizzard Challenge
benchmark.model_or_system: Blizzard Challenge 2020 MH1 entry 'System L' (anonymised system letter; the team's identity was not verified)
benchmark.metric: Pinyin-with-Tone Error Rate (PTER), percent (lower is better), from listener transcription of SUS
benchmark.human_reference: General adult working population of native Mandarin speakers speaking to be understood. The in-test natural-speech reference is a professional voice talent recorded in studio conditions, which is a clearer-than-median speaker.

benchmark.name: Blizzard Challenge
benchmark.model_or_system: VRAIN-UPV MLLP TTS system (System J; non-autoregressive acoustic model + HiFi-GAN)
benchmark.metric: Word error rate (%) from listener transcriptions, Sharvard intelligibility test, task 2021-SH1 (lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult speakers reading sentences aloud in a work setting (native European Spanish speakers). The natural-speech reference in Blizzard is a professional voice talent, who is somewhat above the median speaker.

benchmark.name: Blizzard Challenge
benchmark.model_or_system: VRAIN-UPV MLLP TTS system (Blizzard Challenge 2021 hub task 2021-SH1)
benchmark.metric: word error rate (%) from human listener transcriptions, Sharvard intelligibility test; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce who speak as part of their jobs, reading prepared Spanish text aloud. The in-test natural-speech reference is a professional voice talent recorded in studio conditions, which likely sits at or somewhat above median worker clarity.

benchmark.name: Blizzard Challenge
benchmark.model_or_system: Samsung Speech Synthesis System (Blizzard Challenge 2023 System J; FastSpeech-based acoustic model + HiFi-GAN vocoder)
benchmark.metric: Mean word error rate (%) from human transcription of semantically unpredictable sentences, Hub task FH1; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult native French speakers reading text aloud clearly in quiet conditions. The benchmark's own natural-speech reference is a professional voice talent, who is somewhat clearer than the median adult.

benchmark.name: Seed-TTS-eval
benchmark.metric: Word error rate (%) on Seed-TTS-eval test-en, lower is better; audio transcribed by Whisper-large-v3
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical fluent adults reading short sentences aloud, as represented by the Common Voice volunteer recordings used as the human reference.

benchmark.name: Seed-TTS-eval
benchmark.metric: Word error rate (%) on Seed-TTS-eval test-en, transcribed by Whisper-large-v3; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult working population speaking read text aloud. This is proxied by the benchmark's human reference recordings, which come from crowdsourced, Common Voice-style speakers with varied accents and recording conditions.

benchmark.name: Seed-TTS-Eval
benchmark.metric: Word error rate (%) on the Seed-TTS-Eval test-en split; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult speakers reading short English sentences aloud, as represented by the Common Voice speakers in the test-en references. This is a mixed population of native and non-native speakers with varied recording conditions, which is a reasonable stand-in for ordinary workplace speakers.
